newsitem.title: USA: Clinton pushes for Caribbean trade in budget deal.
newsitem.headline: Clinton pushes for Caribbean trade in budget deal.

text.p: The White House said Tuesday it was pressing Congress to include a tax break on imports from Caribbean countries in the budget package agreed to by President Clinton and Congress.
"We're trying here at the last hour to really get the Caribbean Basin Initiative in this bill," said John Hilley, Clinton's legislative affairs director.

The administration had been pushing to include the measure that would give Caribbean Basin Initiative (CBI) countries parity with North American Free Trade Agreement members, particularly Mexico, on some of their exports to the United States.

The budget plan agreed to by the White House and Congressional leaders did not include the measure. But White House officials said they hoped to get it in the budget legislation before it is voted on by the House and Senate. Votes are expected later this week before lawmakers take their summer recess.

"The president is active on this today," Hilley said about the measure at a White House news conference on the tax and spending package. "There are a number of phone calls by senior administration officials to the trade and tax writing committees that are ongoing."
The CBI was launched in 1983 to provide incentives to invest in Caribbean countries and promote trade and a number of U.S. apparel companies have invested in the region.
The region has said that it has lost investment and market share to Mexico because of the North American Free Trade Agreement, staring with the closure of some 150 apparel plants.
Hilley said Clinton is committed to providing parity to those Caribbean countries hurt by the loss of trade because of NAFTA, which combines Mexico, the United States and Canada in a trading bloc.
"It's something that the president cares deeply about," Hilley said. "It's time to do it."
